title: How to Prevent Condensation on Windows

seo.title: How to Prevent Condensation on Windows
seo.meta_description: Prevent window condensation by controlling indoor humidity, exhausting moisture, improving airflow at the glass, and addressing very cold window surfaces when needed.
seo.search_intent: Resolve the household problem clearly and safely by identifying likely causes and practical next steps.

excerpt: There are two basic ways to reduce window condensation: lower indoor moisture or keep the interior glass surface warmer. Many homes need a little of both.
content_html:
Window condensation is not really a glass-cleaning problem. You have to change the conditions that put the glass below the dew point: too much indoor moisture, a very cold surface, or both.

Measure indoor humidity first

Use a hygrometer and see whether condensation lines up with high readings. If humidity rises after showers, cooking, or indoor clothes drying, start with source control and exhaust.

Use exhaust fans effectively

A bathroom fan should discharge outdoors. Run it during the shower and for a while afterward. Use outdoor-venting kitchen exhaust when cooking creates heavy steam.

Let room air reach the glass

Avoid sealing windows behind heavy curtains all day in cold weather, and do not block all circulation with furniture. Opening blinds or curtains for part of the day can help warm the interior surface.

Do not confuse ventilation with always opening a window

Brief ventilation can help during cold, dry weather. During humid outdoor conditions, opening windows may add moisture. Use outdoor conditions rather than a fixed rule.

Dry water that has already formed

Wipe droplets from frames and sills. Do not leave wood, seals, paint, or drywall wet day after day while you work on the cause.

When the window itself is part of the problem

Very cold glass, conductive frames, and air leakage can encourage condensation. Appropriate weatherstripping, better glazing, or insulation improvements can raise interior surface temperatures. Do not block designed drainage paths.

Do not raise the thermostat just to dry windows

More heat can raise glass temperature, but it also increases energy use and does not correct excessive indoor moisture. Address showers, cooking, indoor drying, leaks, and exhaust before using whole-house temperature as the main fix.

Compare rooms instead of treating every window the same

If condensation affects only one bedroom, compare door position, occupancy, curtains, and airflow. If it affects nearly every window, the cause is more likely house-wide humidity, very cold weather, or the thermal performance of the windows.

The durable fix changes humidity and surface temperature instead of only wiping the glass every morning.

faq.question: Will a dehumidifier help window condensation?
faq.answer: Yes, when excessive indoor humidity is part of the cause.

faq.question: Should I open the window every day?
faq.answer: It depends on outdoor conditions; humid outdoor air can make the problem worse.

faq.question: Can I seal every hole in a window frame?
faq.answer: No. Some openings are intentional drainage paths and should remain clear.
